newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ welcomes govt panel plan on its independence.
newsitem.headline: BOJ welcomes govt panel plan on its independence.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) welcomes a proposal by a government panel to give it more independence, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Thursday.
"The proposal could help the BOJ's efforts to reform itself towards the 21st century, and we highly evaluate it," he said.

Matsushita said the "accountability" of the Bank of Japan would be heavier when the revised law was enacted. "Accountability" is generally regarded as the responsibility of the BOJ to account for what it does.

A government panel earlier on Thursday unveiled final proposals for reforming the law governing the BOJ aiming to boost its independence in forming its monetary policy and transparency in its decision-making process.
Asked if the proposals would restrict the BOJ's independence in monetary policy, Matsushita said various efforts had been made to increase the BOJ's independence.
"Basically, the proposals have been designed so as not to present any obstacles to the BOJ's independence," he said.
Under the proposals, the government could ask the BOJ's policy-making board to delay decisions on monetary policy and the board could decide whether or not to accede to such requests.
Matsushita said there were safeguards in the proposals to check excessive government intervention in the BOJ's policy-making process.
